traces.original: To assess how input rasterization affects detection accuracy and latency, Table~\ref{tab:encoding} compares four distinct BEV representations under identical MobilePIXORNeXt backbone and single-head architecture. TriBand-BEV~\cite{khoshkdahan2026triband} partitions points into three coarse height bands; while it delivers the highest inference throughput ($188.4\,\text{FPS}$) and lowest Host-to-Device transfer payload ($6.76\,\text{MB}$), its Moderate mAP drops to $44.42\%$ ($-5.72\%$ below Strata-BEV14). The lack of continuous elevation moments and horizontal subcell centroid offsets degrades small object localization (Pedestrian AP $38.05\%$, Cyclist AP $21.12\%$). Conventional 35-channel binary occupancy slicing (A1) achieves $47.60\%$ mAP but requires transferring $78.85\,\text{MB}$ per scan, imposing significant Host-to-Device transfer latency ($40.63\,\text{ms}$) while still discarding sub-voxel point coordinates. The 8-channel Strata-BEV8 representation (A2) yields comparable accuracy ($47.37\%$) with fewer channels. In contrast, our 14-channel Strata-BEV14 representation (A3) achieves the highest Moderate mAP of $50.14\%$ ($+5.72\%$ over TriBand-BEV and $+2.54\%$ over Binary35) at $169.0\,\text{FPS}$. Continuous vertical spatial moments ($z_{\max}, z_{\mathrm{mean}}, z_{\mathrm{span}}, z_{\mathrm{std}}$) and subcell centroid displacement offsets $(\Delta\bar{x}, \Delta\bar{y})$ retain critical 3D geometry otherwise lost through horizontal discretization without incurring PointNet encoder overhead.

TriBand-BEV~\cite{khoshkdahan2026triband} partitions points into three coarse height bands; while it delivers the highest inference throughput ($188.4\,\text{FPS}$) and lowest Host-to-Device transfer payload ($6.76\,\text{MB}$), its Moderate mAP drops to $44.42\%$ ($-5.72\%$ below Strata-BEV14). The lack of continuous elevation moments and horizontal subcell centroid offsets degrades small object localization (Pedestrian AP $38.05\%$, Cyclist AP $21.12\%$). Conventional 35-channel binary occupancy slicing (A1) achieves $47.60\%$ mAP but requires transferring $78.85\,\text{MB}$ per scan, imposing significant Host-to-Device transfer latency ($40.63\,\text{ms}$) while still discarding sub-voxel point coordinates. traces.original: {\footnotesize \textit{Note.} All variants share the identical MobilePIXORNeXt-S backbone, F24 SumFPN neck, single-head H16, standard augmentation, and baseline Smooth-L1 loss. Standalone inference speed is measured in FP32 on an NVIDIA L4 GPU under batch size 1 ($800 \times 704$ input grid). TriBand-BEV~\cite{khoshkdahan2026triband} provides the fastest forward execution ($188.43\,\text{FPS}$) due to its compact 3-channel input ($6.76\,\text{MB}$), but suffers significant accuracy degradation ($44.42\%$ Moderate mAP) due to the lack of continuous elevation moments and horizontal subcell centroid offsets. Strata-BEV14 achieves the highest accuracy ($50.14\%$ Moderate mAP and $52.00\%$ $\text{mAP}_9$) while maintaining real-time throughput ($169.01\,\text{FPS}$) and reducing H2D memory payload by $60.0\%$ relative to Binary35 ($31.54\,\text{MB}$ vs. $78.85\,\text{MB}$).}
